about: In Savigny-en-Véron, where the Vienne flows toward the Loire, the Raffault family has farmed for generations. Olga married fellow grower Pierre Raffault in 1931. Asparagus from the sandy local soils was their main crop at first, alongside three hectares of vines. After Pierre’s death in 1947 she kept the estate going. Today her granddaughter Sylvie, Sylvie’s husband Éric de la Vigerie and their son Arnaud farm about 25 hectares of certified-organic vineyards, and the domaine is one of Chinon’s traditional reference points.

Les Picasses is their most famous vineyard: Cabernet Franc vines more than fifty years old, on a south-facing slope above the Vienne’s north bank, rooted in clay over chalky tuffeau. The winemaking has barely changed. The grapes are picked by hand and fermented in stainless steel, then the wine ages slowly in large, neutral casks of oak and sometimes chestnut. It is held back and released about four years after the vintage, so it arrives already showing some development.

The 2019 is dark and spicy, with black currant, blackberry and Morello cherry, prune, licorice and cocoa. With firm tannins and Chinon’s fresh acidity, Les Picasses has a reputation for ageing for decades, and older vintages develop notes of earth, leather and tobacco. It is a classic partner for roast meats, game and dishes cooked over a wood fire.
facts: Large neutral oak (sometimes chestnut); released about four years after vintage
